title: Welfare-Budgeted Adaptive Experiments and Honest Interval Width for Targeting Gains
banked_reason: The promised complete Hölder–margin width frontier was replaced by an implicit one-sided occupation-relaxation lower bound: no explicit full-class branches or thresholds, and no law-independent attaining design and honest interval, are delivered.
gap_reasons: The promised complete Hölder--margin width frontier is replaced by an implicit one-sided occupation-relaxation lower bound: no explicit full-class branches or thresholds, and no law-independent attaining design and honest interval, are delivered.
The suggested saturation/common-realization upgrade restates the unresolved kernel and supplies no concrete proof route for d=1, beta=1, alpha=1/5, rho proportional to T^(3/5).
proof_attempt_summary: The run proved two-direction exposure, class nonemptiness, an all-design coverage-to-information converse, the fixed-gap rho^(-1/2) frontier, and a rigorous baseline-indexed occupation lower relaxation. It failed because the promised full Hölder--margin rate, phase transitions, saturation, and one law-independent attaining design with a connected honest interval remained open; the required early-kill regime had no concrete proof route.
tldr: An adaptive experiment that protects current participants suppresses observations from inferior treatments, while honest inference on the gain from individualized targeting needs those observations and is nonregular near treatment ties. The proved results establish class nonemptiness, the published feasibility rate after a predictable Gaussian-martingale transfer, an all-procedure coverage-to-information converse, and, for sufficiently large horizons in its displayed budget range, the fixed-gap \(\rho^{-1/2}\) frontier. The corrected general construction is a baseline-indexed occupation-measure relaxation: it includes every same-context-law, off-cell-agreeing target-separating alternative, uses exact pointwise Gaussian information, and enforces stochastic context capacity and participant welfare. Every narrow honest procedure must satisfy this relaxation, and its Lagrange lower value obeys weak duality. Saturation, strong duality, an explicit H\"older-local rate, and realization of the baseline-specific profiles by one law-independent adaptive design and connected interval remain open; the \(d=1\), \(\beta=1\), \(\alpha=1/5\), \(\rho\asymp T^{3/5}\) case remains the mandatory early kill test.
gap: Existing regret--inference Pareto results concern point-estimation error for finite-arm treatment gaps or finitely many fixed-gap strata. Praharaj and Khamaru obtain asymptotic Wald inference for fixed linear functionals and near-minimax regret from one linear contextual-bandit design, but not uniform nonregular honest width under a hard welfare budget. Other adaptive confidence-interval results take the logging design as given and target fixed policy values. Optimal-value inference treats the tie nonregularity but does not price exploration by participant welfare. None of these results characterizes the honest expected-width envelope over both designs and common observed-trajectory interval maps.
fill: Positive cumulative exposure identifies the target from the observed trajectory law, whereas an explicit zero-exposure pair proves nonidentification on benchmark-relevant regions. Every reported interval is one common \(P\)-independent Borel map of the observed trajectory, and an explicit constant-gap Gaussian law verifies that both frontier domains are nonempty under mutually compatible primitive constants. The procedure-free coverage reduction makes the extended-valued sequential targeting-gain modulus the lower-bound object. Target-separating local alternative sets generate armwise conditional-Gaussian KL coefficients, a semi-infinite covering program, and a measure-valued dual; the open saturation question asks whether their implicit width level can be realized by welfare-priced predictable exploration and a bias-aware connected interval. The fixed-gap theorem anchors the compulsory branch, and the open kernel requires a matching rate with every threshold derived from primitives.
